title: Career Roadmap: Technician (Defence)
summary: A Defence Technician supports the operation, inspection, maintenance, and repair of technical equipment used by the Indian Armed Forces. Depending on the service, trade, and posting, the work may involve vehicles, weapons-support equipment, electrical systems, communications equipment, aircraft-support systems, engines, or other military machinery.

about.label: Education Pathway
about.text: Defence & Uniformed Services Entry Pathways – Agniveer (Army / Navy / Air Force)

blocks.text: A Defence Technician supports the operation, inspection, maintenance, and repair of technical equipment used by the Indian Armed Forces. Depending on the service, trade, and posting, the work may involve vehicles, weapons-support equipment, electrical systems, communications equipment, aircraft-support systems, engines, or other military machinery.
The role suits candidates interested in practical engineering, troubleshooting, disciplined teamwork, and hands-on technical work.
Potential work environments include:

items.text: Army workshops and equipment-maintenance units
Naval technical and engineering establishments
Air Force technical and ground-support units
Vehicle, electrical, mechanical, and communications maintenance sections
Defence logistics and equipment-support facilities

blocks.label: Important distinction
blocks.text: Agniveer is a recruitment scheme, not one common technician qualification. Army, Navy, and Air Force recruitment have different trade categories and eligibility requirements. An Agniveer appointment does not automatically guarantee a particular technician trade or a permanent defence career.
Recommended qualifications

rows.text: Class 10
May meet eligibility for selected trades, depending on the service notification
Class 12 with Physics, Mathematics, and other prescribed subjects
Relevant to certain technical entries
ITI in an accepted trade
Useful for eligible technical or skilled-trade pathways where accepted
Diploma in Mechanical Engineering
Useful for machinery, vehicle, and equipment maintenance
Diploma in Electrical Engineering
Useful for electrical equipment and power systems
Diploma in Electronics / Electronics and Communication
Useful for communications and electronic equipment
Diploma in Automobile Engineering
Useful for vehicle maintenance and mechanical systems

blocks.text: Eligibility must be verified against the current official recruitment notification. A diploma or ITI qualification does not automatically qualify a candidate for every Agniveer technical category.
Core subjects to learn

items.text: Basic mathematics and applied physics
Engineering drawing and measurement
Mechanical systems and machine components
Electrical circuits and safety
Electronics and troubleshooting
Engines and vehicle systems
Tools, fasteners, bearings, and lubrication
Preventive maintenance
Workplace safety and technical documentation

blocks.text: Indian Army — Agniveer Technical and Related Trades

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Land-based equipment and technical support

Depending on the trade and posting, technical work may involve mechanical equipment, vehicles, electrical systems, or other assigned systems. The Army's Agniveer categories have specific academic and medical requirements.

blocks.label: Official recruitment portal
blocks.text: Join Indian Army
Indian Navy — Agniveer SSR / MR and Relevant Trades

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Naval operations and shipboard or shore support

Navy Agniveer roles differ by entry category. Some technical duties depend on the selected branch, subsequent allocation, and training. Do not assume every Agniveer role is an engineering technician position.

blocks.label: Official recruitment portal
blocks.text: Join Indian Navy
Indian Air Force — Agniveervayu

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Air Force operations and assigned support functions

Technical eligibility depends on the current Agniveervayu notification and the candidate's educational stream. Some duties involve technical support, but a specific aircraft-engineering or maintenance appointment is not guaranteed by entry alone.

blocks.label: Official recruitment portal
blocks.text: Agniveervayu official portal
Stage 1
Complete school education

items.text: Complete Class 10 or Class 12, according to the chosen entry's requirements.
Strengthen mathematics, science, and practical problem-solving.
Research the education, age, height, medical, and physical standards in the relevant notification.
Decide whether your main interest is mechanical, electrical, electronics, vehicle, or general technical work.

blocks.text: Stage 2
Build technical competence

items.text: Learn basic tools, measurements, mechanical components, and electrical safety.
Consider an ITI or diploma where it aligns with the chosen entry's accepted qualifications.
Practise technical drawing, component identification, and systematic fault diagnosis.
Maintain physical fitness and a consistent study schedule.

blocks.text: Stage 3
Prepare for recruitment

items.text: Follow the relevant Army, Navy, or Air Force notification.
Prepare for the prescribed written or online examination.
Practise reasoning, mathematics, science, English, or other subjects included in the applicable syllabus.
Prepare for physical fitness tests, document verification, and medical screening.
Apply only through the official recruitment process.

blocks.text: Stage 4
Complete selection and training

items.text: Clear all prescribed selection stages.
Complete the basic military training and trade-specific training assigned by the service.
Learn equipment handling, maintenance procedures, teamwork, and operational safety.
Qualify for the duties authorised by the service.

blocks.text: Stage 5
Develop technical experience

items.text: Build competence in the assigned trade and equipment.
Follow inspection schedules and maintain accurate service records.
Develop troubleshooting, teamwork, and equipment-care skills.
Plan future qualifications and civilian career options well before the end of the engagement period.

blocks.text: The sequence is a general preparation framework, not a guarantee of recruitment or a specific trade allocation.

rows.text: Mechanical maintenance
Inspect and maintain machinery and mechanical components
Electrical fundamentals
Understand circuits, wiring, power supplies, and electrical safety
Electronics basics
Identify common electronic components and basic faults
Fault diagnosis
Use a structured process to identify equipment problems
Tool handling
Use hand tools and measuring instruments correctly
Preventive maintenance
Follow inspection and servicing schedules
Technical documentation
Record maintenance activities and equipment condition
Safety awareness
Follow approved procedures and use protective equipment
Teamwork
Coordinate maintenance tasks and report faults clearly
Discipline
Follow service rules, instructions, and equipment-control procedures

sections.heading: Tools and Technical Equipment to Learn

blocks.text: Candidates can develop familiarity with general workshop tools and training equipment, including:

items.text: Vernier calipers and micrometers
Multimeters and basic electrical test instruments
Spanners, torque tools, screwdrivers, and pliers
Mechanical drawing and measurement tools
Basic diagnostic equipment for civilian vehicles or training systems
Excel for maintenance logs and inventory records
CAD tools for understanding technical drawings

blocks.text: Training should be carried out under qualified supervision. Military-specific equipment and procedures must be learned through authorised service training.
Depending on the intended entry and future civilian career, consider:

items.text: ITI training in an appropriate trade, such as fitter, electrician, mechanic, or electronics mechanic, if accepted by the target pathway.
Diploma-level technical education in mechanical, electrical, electronics, or automobile engineering.
Workshop safety training and safe use of tools.
Basic first aid and emergency response training.
Computer and documentation skills, including spreadsheets and technical reporting.

blocks.text: Do not pay for a course based on a promise that it guarantees Agniveer selection. Confirm that the qualification is recognised and accepted for the specific recruitment category.
These projects help build technical confidence before applying:

blocks.label: Mechanical Assembly Model
blocks.text: Assemble and document a simple mechanical mechanism.

blocks.label: Electrical Circuit Board
blocks.text: Build a low-voltage training circuit with appropriate supervision.

blocks.label: Preventive Maintenance Checklist
blocks.text: Create a sample inspection schedule for a bicycle, pump, or civilian machine.

blocks.label: Equipment Inventory Spreadsheet
blocks.text: Track components, quantities, inspection dates, and maintenance status.

blocks.label: Basic Fault-Diagnosis Exercise
blocks.text: Identify simulated faults in a safe training circuit or mechanical model.

blocks.label: Technical Drawing Practice
blocks.text: Produce a labelled drawing of a simple mechanical component.
Use civilian or educational equipment for practice; do not attempt to access, modify, or reproduce restricted military systems.
Academic preparation

items.text: Read the official syllabus for the chosen service and entry category.
Practise timed questions in the prescribed subjects.
Revise science and mathematics fundamentals relevant to the role.
Maintain a record of mock-test scores and review recurring mistakes.

blocks.text: Physical preparation

items.text: Build cardiovascular endurance and general strength gradually.
Practise running and bodyweight exercises according to your current fitness level.
Prioritise sleep, recovery, and injury prevention.
Check the official physical standards rather than relying on unofficial estimates.

blocks.text: Document preparation
Keep relevant documents ready as specified in the notification, such as:

items.text: Educational certificates and mark sheets
Identity and date-of-birth documentation
Required category or domicile documents, if applicable
ITI or diploma certificates, where relevant
Other forms and declarations specifically requested by the recruiting authority

blocks.text: Agniveer is generally a four-year engagement under the Agnipath scheme. At the end of the engagement, up to 25% of a particular Agniveer cohort may be selected for regular cadre enrolment, subject to the applicable scheme, organisational requirements, performance, and selection process. Retention is not guaranteed.
Recruitment and Training
Selection, military training, and trade allocation
Agniveer Service
Build operational, technical, and teamwork experience during the engagement period
Possible regular cadre selection
Subject to applicable selection and service requirements
Civilian career transition
Use transferable technical skills and pursue suitable further qualifications
Potential civilian opportunities
Depending on trade experience and additional qualifications, candidates may explore:

items.text: Industrial maintenance technician
Mechanical or electrical technician
Automobile service technician
Electronics service technician
Manufacturing maintenance assistant
Equipment service and field-support technician
Warehouse, inventory, and technical logistics roles

blocks.text: Civilian eligibility depends on the employer's requirements, recognised qualifications, experience, and any required licences. Defence service experience does not automatically substitute for a civilian trade licence.
Preparation progress
Choose the intended service and recruitment category
Read the latest official notification and verify eligibility
Complete the required school education
Build mechanical, electrical, or electronics fundamentals
Prepare for the prescribed written or online examination
Develop fitness for the applicable physical tests
Organise educational and identity documents
Plan technical skill development and post-engagement options

For students targeting a Technician (Defence) career, the first step is to identify the exact service and recruitment category rather than preparing for Army, Navy, and Air Force as if they had identical requirements.
Focus on three priorities:

blocks.label: Eligibility
blocks.text: Match your education and age to the latest official notification.

blocks.label: Technical ability
blocks.text: Build practical mechanical, electrical, or electronics skills relevant to the intended trade.

blocks.label: Recruitment readiness
blocks.text: Prepare academically and physically, while planning for career options after the Agniveer engagement.
A strong candidate combines technical aptitude, physical fitness, discipline, safety awareness, and a realistic understanding of the engagement terms.
